organelles.label: Cell–cell bridge
organelles.plain: Two cells can share cytoplasm through an open bridge lined by continuous membrane and S-layer.

size.text: Cryotomography found widths of 57–162 nm and lengths of 253–2,144 nm. The drawing uses the midpoints of those separate ranges.

organelles.label: S-layer and membrane
organelles.plain: An envelope section shows the protein lattice above the membrane. The gap sets the vertical scale of the drawing.

size.text: In H26 cells, the measured membrane-to-S-layer distance averaged 20.4 nm (±2.7 nm). The patch width and motif spacing are illustrative.

organelles.label: Extracellular vesicle
organelles.plain: A membrane-enclosed particle released into the surrounding medium.

size.text: Electron microscopy of vesicles isolated from Haloferax cultures gave diameters of 50–150 nm.

organelles.label: Archaellum
organelles.plain: This rotating surface appendage propels the cell. The adhesion pilus has its own experimental assembly on the bench.
organelles.no_size: Cryotomography identifies the swimming filament. A complete filament length for this specimen is unreported here.

organelles.label: Possible storage granule
organelles.plain: An electron-dense body in the cytoplasm was tentatively identified as a storage granule. Its contents are unknown.
organelles.no_size: The paper identifies a candidate granule in Fig. 1. Its diameter is unreported here.
